column5: Which group would most people in India associate this surname with?
column7: Which region is it most associated with?

column8: Most people, especially in the Hindi belt, link Yadav with the Yadav community of UP and Bihar, usually counted as OBC. In Bengal the surname is less common, but the North Indian association is the one people know.

This is the English spelling of Chattopadhyay, a Bengali Brahmin surname. In Bengal almost everyone would read it as upper caste. The Bengali spelling given here (চ্যাটার্জি) follows the English form, not the older চট্টোপাধ্যায়.

In West Bengal Bauri is a well-known Scheduled Caste, especially in Bankura, Purulia, Birbhum and nearby districts. Outside Bengal many people would not recognise the name, so the association is strong locally rather than all-India.
People generally connect Paswan with Bihar and with a Scheduled Caste community (Paswan/Dusadh). The name is familiar even outside Bihar because of politics.
English form of Mukhopadhyay, a Bengali Brahmin surname. The usual reading is upper-caste Bengali. Everyday Bengali spelling is মুখোপাধ্যায়; মুখার্জি follows the English spelling.

Almost everyone links Patel with Gujarat, especially the Patidar community, seen as a dominant farming and business group. It is not read as Dalit. Some Patels have asked for OBC status, but the common assumption is a dominant Gujarati caste.

As a surname, most people in North India take Valmiki/Balmiki to mean a Scheduled Caste community. A few may think of the poet Valmiki, but for a family name the community reading is the usual one. Less familiar in Bengal.

Das is very common in Bengal, Odisha and Assam, and also used in North India. In Bengal it is used by Kayasthas and by many other communities, including some Scheduled Caste families. People would not agree on one caste. It sounds eastern, but not only one region.

Singh is used by Rajputs, by many other North Indian castes, and by Sikhs. It does not point to one group. The usual picture is North Indian or Punjabi. In Bengal সিংহ is a different, less common surname and is not what people mean by Singh.
Sharma is widely taken as a Brahmin surname of the Hindi-speaking north. That is the assumption most people would make.
In Uttar Pradesh and nearby states Jatav is commonly known as a Scheduled Caste community. In Bengal the surname is rare; many people here would not know it unless they follow North Indian news.

Ghosh is a very common Bengali surname. In everyday talk people treat it as a forward / bhadralok name, often Kayastha, though not every Ghosh family has the same background. It is not read as Scheduled Caste. The caste link is not as tight as Banerjee or Chatterjee.
Trivedi is generally read as Brahmin (someone connected with the three Vedas). Common in the Hindi belt and also in Gujarat. Most people would say upper caste, North Indian.

Mondal is extremely common in Bengal among many Hindu castes (Mahishya and others, and also some Scheduled Caste families) and among Bengali Muslims. People would place it in Bengal, but not in one caste or community.
